headline: Broad growth lifts earnings and returns, capital eases
summary_short: Wells Fargo earned $5.95B ($1.87 per diluted share, +13% y/y) on revenue of $21.9B, up 2% y/y, as net interest income rose 5% and noninterest expense fell 1%.
summary_long: Net interest income rose 5% y/y on higher loan and securities balances and fixed-rate asset repricing, while noninterest income slipped 1% on lower trading gains, lease income and venture capital results. Expenses fell 1% on efficiency initiatives including an 8% headcount cut. The provision rose to $1,029M on a higher allowance for commercial and auto loans from loan growth. Average loans and deposits each rose 11%. ROTCE was 16.3%. Wells repurchased $2.5B of stock, and CET1 eased to 10.0% from 10.3% last quarter. No numeric guidance was given.
confidence_notes: Release figures are preliminary pending the 10-Q. Third-quarter 2026 tax expense included $170M of discrete benefits; the prior-year quarter included $296M of severance expense. The shard's EPS ($1.87) matches the release. Prior-year EPS in the release is $1.66 (the resolver's SEC basic value is $1.68). No forward guidance was stated.

drivers.explanation: Higher net interest income and fee income were partly offset by lower trading gains, lease income after the rail car leasing sale, and venture capital results.
Higher loan and investment securities balances, balance sheet growth in Markets and fixed-rate asset repricing, partly offset by lower rates on floating-rate assets and higher deposit costs.
Efficiency initiatives including an 8% headcount reduction, lower severance and lower lease expense, partly offset by higher revenue-related compensation and technology costs.
Higher net interest income and lower expenses, plus $170M of discrete tax benefits, partly offset by a higher provision.
Net income growth plus a lower share count; Wells repurchased 28.6 million shares this quarter.
Included an increase in the allowance for credit losses on higher commercial and industrial and auto loan balances, partly offset by a lower commercial real estate allowance.
CEO Charlie Scharf cited broad-based growth, higher earnings and stronger returns, with ROTCE rising to 16.3% and average loans and deposits both up 11% y/y.
